segments.text: Good morning, everyone. Today I'm talking to Gemma Roberts from the Bristol Information Centre.
She is going to tell us about what's going on in Bristol during the next few months.
Hi, Chris.
So, Gemma, what is the most popular attraction in Bristol?
Well, that's difficult to say exactly. There are so many things going on here.
For example, new visitors to Bristol are always fascinated by the Clifton Suspension Bridge.
This was designed by the famous Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunell, who is
also famous for designing Bristol's Temple Meets station, the Great Western Railway,
London Paddington station and the SS Great Britain, to name a few.
By 1843, with only one of the towers completed, the project was abandoned.
Brunel died aged 53 in 1859, but the bridge was only completed in 1864.
Although it was designed for use by light horse-drawn traffic in the Victorian period,
it still copes with 21st century commuter traffic with 11,000 to 12,000 vehicles crossing
it every day.
Yes, it's certainly impressive.
What else do you recommend people go and see in Bristol?
Another popular attraction is the At Bristol Science Centre in Millenium Square by The
Harbourside.
There are many cafes and restaurants here with handy bike racks located nearby and regular
buses and ferries running in the area every day.
The Millenium Car Park provides easy access as in located off the A4.
The centre is a state-of-the-art interactive science centre which offers an amazing world
of hands-on discovery for people of all ages. It shows how the world around us works with
programmes of special exhibitions including travel by air and sea.
Sounds like fun. So what can people do in Bristol if they want an outdoor activity?
If you want to go up and away, you can take a flight with Bristol balloons. This is a
great way to get a better perspective of the Clifton Suspension Bridge over the beautiful
Avon Gorge. On a clear day there may also be the chance for a spectacular view of the
new seven crossing. The flight lasts an hour, chilled champagne is served when the balloon
has touched down before returning back to the launch site. The whole experience takes
between three and four hours.
Exciting stuff. And of course there's the Bristol International Balloon Fiesta.
Yes, this is Europe's largest ballooning event, and an amazing spectacle and free event
for the whole family.
Over 150 hot air balloons will take off from Ashton Court Estate at dawn, and light up
the skies at night, with evening glows, with fun activities on the ground to keep the
family entertained.
The event features four days of extravagant hot air balloon displays, with half a million
visitors coming to watch balloons of all shapes and sizes lift off over the
city. The famous night glow is a stunning sight with 30 ballooning teams lighting
up their balloon as night falls at 9 p.m. on Thursday and Saturday to a
backdrop of spectacular fireworks. What about something for animal lovers in
the city? Well the Bristol Zoo Gardens offers a fun packed day out for all the
family, with over 400 species packed into 12 acres of beautiful manicured gardens. What's
more, you can take the city sightseeing open-top bus tour which stops right outside the zoo
and claim 20% off your zoo entry ticket from the driver. Also, the Bristol Aquarium has
some new residents for 2015, along with their 4,000 other aquatic creatures. Children can
see many varieties of fish, big and small.
